notes: Delete mirror of biology-replace-0020: the rule is removed. New members become not known (the rule was the only route); well-known members keep their value where it was stored by name and become not known where it was reached through the rule. Membership no longer needs to give way, since nothing clashes. R1: there are no freshwater or terrestrial echinoderms; a few tolerate brackish water, which is still sea water. Well-known members: the starfish and the sand dollar, whose names do not contain 'sea' (sea urchin, sea cucumber and sea lily would leak the answer); their habitat is stated by name and leaving the echinoderm class contradicts no firm fact outside the chain. The Chinese prompts name only the class (棘皮动物); 海星 for starfish would leak, so no member appears in Chinese. New members are named only as echinoderms: the prompts leave out 'brittle star', 'crinoid/feather star', 'Antarctic' and 'seamount', which would give the sea away by another route. Residual risk: a model that recognises the genus as a brittle star or crinoid could reach the sea by that subclass, but neither name is known enough to matter ('Promachocrinus fragarius' 0 hits, 'Ophiojura exbodi' 40). Near query asks the class's symmetry (five-fold), which differs from 'fresh water'. Verifier: in the delete the genus route has no clash to block it: 'Ophiojura' (160) is mostly the 2021 'Jurassic brittle star' news and '-crinus' marks a crinoid, so a model that parses the genus could keep 'in the sea'. Accepted as small, as with the jumping spider in 0005.
